title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: PhysioOpenSim provides R interface OpenSim biomechanics simulation analysis. package supports two execution backends: Native – OpenSim C++ libraries linked compile time (fastest) CLI – OpenSim command-line tool invoked external process (portable) backends accessed high-level R functions, user code need change switching backends.

title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: Start verifying capabilities available installation. neither backend available, can still use template system (described ) prepare OpenSim setup files later execution.
code: library(PhysioOpenSim)  # Native C++ support compiled in? opensimAvailable() #> [1] FALSE  # Detailed build configuration cfg <- opensimBuildConfig() str(cfg) #> List of 3 #>  $ package        : chr "PhysioOpenSim" #>  $ opensim_enabled: logi FALSE #>  $ detect_method  : chr "none" # Is the OpenSim CLI on your PATH? opensimCLIAvailable() #> [1] FALSE

title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: native support available, can load inspect .osim model files directly R.
code: # Load a model model <- opensimLoadModel("gait2392.osim")  # Inspect the model opensimModelName(model) info <- opensimModelSummary(model) str(info) # List of 8 #  $ model_name   : chr "gait2392" #  $ n_bodies     : int 14 #  $ n_joints     : int 13 #  $ n_markers    : int 35 #  $ n_muscles    : int 92 #  $ n_coordinates: int 37 #  $ total_mass   : num 75.2 #  $ initialized  : logi FALSE  # Component names comps <- opensimModelComponents(model) head(comps$muscles)  # Modify and save opensimSetModelName(model, "my_custom_model") opensimModelInitialize(model) opensimSaveModel(model, "my_custom_model.osim")

title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: template system lets generate OpenSim tool setup XMLs template replacing specific XML tag values. works without OpenSim installation.
code: # Create a simple template tpl <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>',   "<OpenSimDocument>",   "  <InverseKinematicsTool>",   "    <model_file>Unassigned</model_file>",   "    <marker_file>Unassigned</marker_file>",   "    <time_range>0 1</time_range>",   "  </InverseKinematicsTool>",   "</OpenSimDocument>" ), tpl)  # Generate a configured setup file out <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") result <- opensimWriteToolSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = tpl,   output_file = out,   fields = list(     model_file = "gait2392.osim",     marker_file = "walking_trial.trc",     time_range = "0.5 2.0"   ) )  # What was applied? result$applied_tags #> [1] "model_file"  "marker_file" "time_range" result$missing_tags #> character(0)  # Inspect the output cat(readLines(result$output_file), sep = "\n") #> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?> #> <OpenSimDocument> #>   <InverseKinematicsTool> #>     <model_file>gait2392.osim</model_file> #>     <marker_file>walking_trial.trc</marker_file> #>     <time_range>0.5 2.0</time_range> #>   </InverseKinematicsTool> #> </OpenSimDocument>

title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: default, strict = TRUE causes error requested tag found template. Use strict = FALSE partial replacements.
code: tpl2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   "<root>",   "  <model_file>old</model_file>",   "</root>" ), tpl2)  # This would error with strict = TRUE: out2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") result2 <- suppressWarnings(   opensimWriteToolSetupFromTemplate(     template_file = tpl2,     output_file = out2,     fields = list(model_file = "new.osim", nonexistent_tag = "value"),     strict = FALSE   ) ) result2$applied_tags #> [1] "model_file" result2$missing_tags #> [1] "nonexistent_tag"

title: Getting Started with PhysioOpenSim
text: setup XML, run OpenSim. Typed wrappers available common tools:
code: # Auto-selects native or CLI backend result <- opensimRunTool("ik_setup.xml") result$status    # 0 = success result$stdout result$stderr  # Force CLI with extra arguments result <- opensimRunTool(   "ik_setup.xml",   execution = "cli",   extra_args = c("--visualize"),   timeout_sec = 120 ) opensimRunIK("ik_setup.xml") opensimRunID("id_setup.xml") opensimRunSO("so_setup.xml") opensimRunAnalyze("analyze_setup.xml") opensimRunRRA("rra_setup.xml") opensimRunCMC("cmc_setup.xml")

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: common OpenSim workflow chains multiple tools sequence: Inverse Kinematics (IK) – Compute joint angles marker data Inverse Dynamics (ID) – Compute joint moments kinematics + forces Static Optimization () – Estimate muscle forces joint moments PhysioOpenSim’s template system tool runners make straightforward script pipeline entirely R.

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: vignette assumes : OpenSim model file (.osim) Marker trajectory data (.trc) External forces data (.mot .xml) Template XML files tool

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: Generate IK setup template, run .
code:
library(PhysioOpenSim)  # Create dummy files for demonstration model_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".osim") marker_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".trc") writeLines("dummy", model_file) writeLines("dummy", marker_file)  # Create an IK template ik_tpl <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>',   '<OpenSimDocument Version="40000">',   '  <InverseKinematicsTool name="ik">',   '    <model_file>Unassigned</model_file>',   '    <marker_file>Unassigned</marker_file>',   '    <output_motion_file>Unassigned</output_motion_file>',   '    <time_range>0 1</time_range>',   '    <results_directory>./</results_directory>',   '  </InverseKinematicsTool>',   '</OpenSimDocument>' ), ik_tpl)  ik_output <- tempfile(fileext = ".mot") ik_setup <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml")  ik_result <- opensimWriteIKSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = ik_tpl,   output_file = ik_setup,   model_file = model_file,   marker_file = marker_file,   output_motion_file = ik_output,   time_range = c(0.5, 2.0),   results_directory = tempdir() )  cat("Applied tags:", paste(ik_result$applied_tags, collapse = ", "), "
") #> Applied tags: model_file, marker_file, output_motion_file, time_range, results_directory # Execute IK (requires OpenSim) ik_run <- opensimRunIK(ik_setup) cat("IK exit status:", ik_run$status, "
") cat("IK elapsed:", round(ik_run$elapsed_sec, 2), "sec
")

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: ID uses IK output input coordinates.
code: # Create an ID template id_tpl <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>',   '<OpenSimDocument Version="40000">',   '  <InverseDynamicsTool name="id">',   '    <model_file>Unassigned</model_file>',   '    <coordinates_file>Unassigned</coordinates_file>',   '    <output_gen_force_file>Unassigned</output_gen_force_file>',   '    <time_range>0 1</time_range>',   '    <lowpass_cutoff_frequency_for_coordinates>-1</lowpass_cutoff_frequency_for_coordinates>',   '    <results_directory>./</results_directory>',   '  </InverseDynamicsTool>',   '</OpenSimDocument>' ), id_tpl)  # IK output becomes ID input -- create a dummy for the demo ik_output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".mot") writeLines("dummy", ik_output_file)  id_output <- tempfile(fileext = ".sto") id_setup <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml")  id_result <- opensimWriteIDSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = id_tpl,   output_file = id_setup,   model_file = model_file,   coordinates_file = ik_output_file,   output_gen_force_file = id_output,   time_range = c(0.5, 2.0),   lowpass_cutoff_frequency_for_coordinates = 6 )  cat("Applied tags:", paste(id_result$applied_tags, collapse = ", "), "\n") #> Applied tags: model_file, coordinates_file, output_gen_force_file, lowpass_cutoff_frequency_for_coordinates, time_range # Execute ID id_run <- opensimRunID(id_setup) cat("ID exit status:", id_run$status, "\n")

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: uses coordinates ID.
code: # Create an SO template so_tpl <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>',   '<OpenSimDocument Version="40000">',   '  <StaticOptimization name="so">',   '    <model_file>Unassigned</model_file>',   '    <coordinates_file>Unassigned</coordinates_file>',   '    <time_range>0 1</time_range>',   '    <results_directory>./</results_directory>',   '  </StaticOptimization>',   '</OpenSimDocument>' ), so_tpl)  so_setup <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml")  so_result <- opensimWriteSOSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = so_tpl,   output_file = so_setup,   model_file = model_file,   coordinates_file = ik_output_file,   time_range = c(0.5, 2.0),   results_directory = tempdir() )  cat("Applied tags:", paste(so_result$applied_tags, collapse = ", "), "\n") #> Applied tags: model_file, coordinates_file, time_range, results_directory # Execute SO so_run <- opensimRunSO(so_setup) cat("SO exit status:", so_run$status, "\n")

title: OpenSim Tool Pipeline: IK to ID to SO
text: practice run three steps sequentially.
code: # Full pipeline ik <- opensimRunIK(ik_setup) stopifnot(ik$status == 0)  id <- opensimRunID(id_setup) stopifnot(id$status == 0)  so <- opensimRunSO(so_setup) stopifnot(so$status == 0)  cat("Pipeline complete.\n")

title: Native OpenSim C++ Integration for PhysioExperiment
text: Native OpenSim C++ Integration PhysioExperiment PhysioOpenSim provides direct access OpenSim musculoskeletal modeling library R via Rcpp, without requiring Python Java bridges. package wraps model-level operations simulation tool execution seamless integration biomechanics analysis workflows within PhysioExperiment ecosystem. OpenSim linkage optional build time. OpenSim C++ SDK detected, package installs fallback mode informative runtime messages, ensuring dependent packages can still loaded.

title: Native OpenSim C++ Integration for PhysioExperiment
text: PhysioOpenSim automatically locates OpenSim SDK install time using two strategies (checked order): pkg-config – pkg-config opensim OPENSIM_HOME – environment variable pointing OpenSim installation root (inspects include/sdk/include lib/sdk/lib) neither method succeeds, package builds fallback mode: opensimAvailable() returns FALSE OpenSim-dependent calls return descriptive error.

title: Native OpenSim C++ Integration for PhysioExperiment
text: tool wrapper supports three execution backends selected execution argument: "native" – calls OpenSim C++ API directly (requires native-enabled build) "cli" – invokes opensim-cmd run-tool subprocess "auto" (default) – uses native available, otherwise falls back CLI wrappers return structured list containing execution backend used, stdout, stderr, exit status, elapsed time pipeline logging reproducibility.

title: Native OpenSim C++ Integration for PhysioExperiment
code: library(PhysioOpenSim)  # --- Check availability --- opensimAvailable() #> [1] TRUE opensimBuildConfig() #> $detect_method #> [1] "OPENSIM_HOME" #> $include_path #> [1] "/opt/opensim/sdk/include" #> ...  # --- Load and inspect a model --- model <- opensimLoadModel("gait2392.osim") opensimModelName(model) #> [1] "gait2392" opensimModelSummary(model) #> Bodies: 13, Joints: 13, Muscles: 92, Markers: 35  # --- Initialize for simulation --- opensimModelInitialize(model) opensimFinalizeConnections(model)  # --- Batch-process IK from a template --- ik_setup <- opensimWriteIKSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = "templates/ik_setup.xml",   output_file   = "run/trial01_ik_setup.xml",   model_file    = "model/gait2392.osim",   marker_file   = "data/trial01.trc",   output_motion_file = "results/trial01_ik.mot",   time_range    = c(0.5, 1.5) )  # --- Run Inverse Kinematics --- result <- opensimRunIK(ik_setup$output_file, fail_on_error = FALSE) result$execution #> [1] "native" result$status #> [1] 0 result$elapsed #> [1] 2.34  # --- Backend selection --- result_cli <- opensimRunIK("setup_ik.xml", execution = "cli") result_nat <- opensimRunIK("setup_ik.xml", execution = "native")

code: # Create a minimal template in a temp file tpl <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(c(   "<OpenSimDocument>",   "  <model_file>Unassigned</model_file>",   "  <time_range>0 1</time_range>",   "</OpenSimDocument>" ), tpl)  out <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") result <- opensimWriteToolSetupFromTemplate(   template_file = tpl,   output_file = out,   fields = list(model_file = "my_model.osim", time_range = "0.5 2.0") ) result$applied_tags #> [1] "model_file" "time_range" readLines(result$output_file) #> [1] "<OpenSimDocument>"                        #> [2] "  <model_file>my_model.osim</model_file>" #> [3] "  <time_range>0.5 2.0</time_range>"       #> [4] "</OpenSimDocument>"

title: PhysioOpenSim 0.1.2
text: Fixed non-portable assertion OpenSim parity test (test-opensim-parity.R) broke Windows binary builds. setup writer normalizes output paths via normalizePath(mustWork = FALSE), leaves non-existent relative path unchanged Linux/macOS absolutizes Windows; test now matches <output_gen_force_file> tag basename passes platforms. change package behaviour.

title: PhysioOpenSim 0.1.1
text: Added OpenSim parity fixture test (VAL-06). PhysioOpenSim thin wrapper whose native model parser CLI tools require OpenSim-enabled build, fully OpenSim-free numeric parity impossible; new always-running check validates pure-R setup writer real OpenSim: OpenSim’s InverseDynamicsTool loads PhysioOpenSim-generated ID setup reads numeric fields (time_range, lowpass) back exactly (recorded bundled reference). bundled real model (inst/extdata/arm26.osim, opensim-models) plus OpenSim summary now back native-parser parity OpenSim-enabled builds, replacing PHYSIO_OPENSIM_MODEL env var. Generated data-raw/opensim_reference.{R,py} (OpenSim 4.6).

title: PhysioOpenSim 0.1.0
text: Initial release standalone package x-biosignal (PhysioExperiment) ecosystem. PhysioOpenSim provides native OpenSim C++ bridge R via Rcpp, exposing model-level operations full-tool execution support biomechanics workflows. OpenSim linkage optional build time; OpenSim detected, package still installs OpenSim-dependent calls fail informative runtime errors.

title: PhysioOpenSim 0.1.0
text: opensimAvailable() reports whether package compiled OpenSim headers libraries linked, opensimBuildConfig() returns detection method compilation status. opensimCLIPath() resolves opensim-cmd executable (via argument, OPENSIM_CLI environment variable, PATH) opensimCLIAvailable() checks resolvability without raising error. opensimLoadModel() loads .osim model PhysioOpenSimModel handle, opensimModelInitialize() opensimModelIsInitialized() managing system state. opensimModelSummary() returns structural metadata (body, joint, marker, muscle, coordinate counts plus total mass) file path loaded handle, opensimModelComponents() lists corresponding component names. opensimModelName(), opensimSetModelName(), opensimFinalizeConnections(), opensimSaveModel() inspect, rename, finalize connections , serialize model back XML. opensimRunTool() runs tool setup XML, returning structured result execution mode, status, captured stdout/stderr, elapsed time, supporting working directory, extra CLI arguments, timeout, optional fail--error. Tool-specific wrappers opensimRunIK(), opensimRunID(), opensimRunSO(), opensimRunAnalyze(), opensimRunCMC(), opensimRunRRA() cover inverse kinematics, inverse dynamics, static optimization, analysis, computed muscle control, residual reduction algorithm. opensimWriteToolSetupFromTemplate() performs tag replacement strict permissive handling missing tags reports applied missing tags. Convenience wrappers opensimWriteIKSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteIDSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteSOSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteAnalyzeSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteRRASetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteCMCSetupFromTemplate() normalize model, motion, marker, loads paths accept optional time range results directory tool.
